steps: Assume SAT has size n^c circuits. Substitute the circuit into each L_N-bit generated query of H_N and charge the generator once, giving the beta-zero transfer bound.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No named proof system in the current packet proves DirectClusterSound(C,k) from ordinary soundness, local consistency, or bounded projection treewidth alone.
steps: Instantiate Psys as a row-local projection-CSP verifier for beta-zero XOR certificates; rows query target coordinates Q_r and proof variables P_r.
For a candidate cluster C, form Phi_C(T|_{U_C},z), the existential CSP describing simultaneous acceptance of all rows in C under a projected proof view z.
Completeness gives Phi_C(H_N^SAT|_{U_C},z*) for some z*, hence P_C is nonempty.
If |U_C|=O(log N), P_C has density at least 2^{-|U_C|}=N^{-O(1)} among all N-bit truth tables.
If the projection-decision width is O(log N), membership in P_C is decidable in N^{O(1)} time, so the property is constructive.
To make P_C useful against SIZE_{m_N}(N^k), one needs DirectClusterSound(C,k), excluding every small circuit truth table from the projected accepting set.
Ordinary soundness only excludes globally consistent accepting proofs; the odd-charge Tseitin embedding supplies locally satisfying proof views for every target table on proper clusters.
Sparse residual compression shows that any certificate whose row selection leaves only a small exceptional set also leaks a nonuniform patching circuit for H_N.

assumptions: Model: nonuniform Boolean circuits over m_N input bits, size threshold N^k, with no hidden row-selection advice beyond O(log N) uniformly recoverable public parameters.
Regime: |U_C|<=a log N and d_N<=b log N for constants a,b independent of N and of the target circuit.
Constructivity: from N and C, the projected predicate Phi_C(T|_{U_C},z) is decidable in N^{O(1)} time by enumerating or dynamic-programming over the width-d_N proof-view representation.
Completeness: the actual H_N^SAT projection is accepted by some proof-view assignment z*, so the property is nonempty and contains the source object.
Usefulness: DirectClusterSound is semantic over all small circuit truth tables, not merely ordinary verifier soundness for a fixed global proof.
definitions: source object: H_N^SAT is the beta-zero XOR truth table on N coordinates, H_N(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)), with M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, SAT query length L_N=(log N)^d, and generator overhead N^{rho+o(1)}.
target object: P_C is the truth-table property accepted by the projected row-cluster CSP Phi_C(T|_{U_C},z) for N-bit tables T, targeting SIZE_{m_N}(N^k) where m_N=ceil(log N).
controlled interface: a uniform Psys row cluster C whose verifier rows query target coordinates Q_r and proof variables, with U_C=union_{r in C}Q_r and projected existential decision width d_N.

target-preserving condition: DirectClusterSound(C,k) holds, meaning every SIZE_{m_N}(N^k) circuit truth table makes Phi_C unsatisfiable for all proof-view assignments, while H_N^SAT has an accepting projected proof view.

equations.valid_when: Valid when the certificate carrier is represented by adaptive summaries, openings, and transcript control costs in one unrestricted circuit model.

equations.label: beta0_cover_predictor_size
equations.valid_when: Valid when each queried SAT label is opened by the same advice-free adaptive cover and M_N is at most N^{q+o(1)}.

equations.label: row_residual_patch
equations.valid_when: Applies after D_N agrees with H_N^{SAT} off R_N and residual inputs may be hardwired in unrestricted circuits.

equations.label: source_lower_bound_falsifier
equations.valid_when: Requires the claimed lower bound to target the same explicit beta-zero XOR family and the same unrestricted circuit size measure.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Escape requires proving alpha_ad>=a-q-o(1), or |R_N|>=N^{a-1-o(1)}, or showing the certificate is genuinely nonfunctional and cannot be converted into label openings or a predictor for H_N^{SAT}.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Finite route-specific falsifier for low-cover beta-zero MCSP/MKtP certificate carriers; it supports the row-residual packet without claiming P != NP.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let H_N^{SAT}(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)) with M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, query length L_N=(log N)^d, and generator size N^{rho+o(1)}. If a Psys/MCSP/MKtP certificate carrier computes the queried SAT labels through an advice-free adaptive cover of exponent alpha_ad except on a residual R_N of size N^{r+o(1)}, then C(H_N^{SAT})<=N^{max{rho,q+alpha_ad,r+1}+o(1)}. Hence any claimed source lower bound C(H_N^{SAT})>N^a is falsified when max{rho,q+alpha_ad,r+1}<a.

assumptions: The carrier may have existential hard witnesses but also easy accepted witnesses.
Nonuniform advice selecting a hard witness is not allowed unless the target claim is explicitly nonuniform.
Canonical unranking is permitted only when accepted distinct-image entropy D is bounded and computable in E time.
definitions: source object: accepted certificate set A_N with emitted rows T_N(c) and a hardness predicate LB(T_N(c),2^{theta N}).
target object: an advice-free explicit language lower bound obtained by searching or multiplexing accepted rows.
controlled interface: selector Sel_N, canonical unranking map, or image-entropy quotient used to locate a hard row.
target-preserving condition: row selection must be E-uniform or its information cost must be included in the target length and exponent ledger.

equations.label: multiplexed_extraction_rate
equations.valid_when: Valid when distinct accepted images admit E-canonical unranking and the kappa-gap padding preserves all target lengths.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A single b_N-bit hard-row selector not generated in E is a falsifier unless b_N is absorbed into D or the claim is downgraded to a nonuniform statement.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Advice-leakage audit for hard-row selection before any MCSP carrier consequence is promoted.
candidate_lemmas.statement: An MCSP/MKtP carrier that only asserts an accepted hard row chosen by a nonuniform selector does not target-preserve an E-language or NP lower-bound consequence. It is valid for the route only after either an advice-free selector is supplied or the accepted-image entropy is charged in the multiplexed target.

assumptions: Ordinary local consistency or cluster soundness is insufficient unless it excludes every unrestricted circuit below threshold.
Dense polynomial-time decidable projections that exclude small circuits trigger the natural-property falsifier under standard PRF assumptions.
Sparse generated certificates remain outside known naturalness only if indexed openings and adaptive covers are above the claimed threshold.
definitions: source object: semantic lower-bound certificate pi for a beta-zero XOR row or SAT-query table.
target object: sound implication LB(row,2^{theta N}) in the unrestricted circuit model.
controlled interface: transformation from pi to either a functional opener, a residual predictor, or a direct proof of anti-ball distance from all small circuits.
target-preserving condition: the transformation uses no advice, no dense projection, and no change from unrestricted circuits to a restricted proof model.

equations.label: escape_threshold
equations.latex: \alpha_{ad}\ge \theta-o(1)\ \text{ for direct row hardness, or }\ q+\alpha_{ad}\ge a-o(1)\ \text{ for beta-zero XOR hardness}
equations.valid_when: Valid when the certificate escape is tested against the same unrestricted row-hardness threshold or beta-zero XOR lower-bound exponent.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If pi can be projected to a polynomial-time dense useful property or opened by alpha_ad below threshold, the route is quarantined rather than promoted.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier-typing and escape-condition lemma for nonfunctional certificate proposals.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A nonfunctional Psys certificate can escape the adaptive-cover upper bound only if its soundness implication proves row hardness without yielding a low-cover predictor for H_N^{SAT} or a sparse residual correction. This escape is non-natural only when the accepted certificate family remains sparse or nonconstructive in the relevant truth-table universe.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if no named Psys certificate model yields either functional label openings, sparse residual agreement, or a formal high-cover escape condition.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only after proving the low-cover residual theorem for a named Psys, recording prior-art boundaries, and producing a pvsnp_inference_quality packet with the exponents a,q,rho,alpha_ad,r.
control_decision.reason: The branch improved the atlas obligation by attaching the adaptive-cover obstruction to the exact beta-zero source family and quantitative residual thresholds.

dependency_updates.description: Low-cover MCSP/MKtP carriers now have an exact beta-zero falsifier threshold q+alpha_ad<a and residual threshold r+1<a.
The prior carrier-to-E extraction remains valid only after the source survives adaptive-cover, residual, and selector-advice audits.
Residual exceptions may be hardwired for an unrestricted upper-bound contradiction, but hard-row selection for a target language must be advice-free or entropy-charged.
The sparse-row residual lemma and adaptive-cover cap are combined into one exponent comparison for H_N^{SAT}.

falsifiers: falsifier: alpha_ad<a-q-o(1) and |R_N|<N^{a-1-o(1)} give an explicit unrestricted circuit below the claimed source lower bound.
falsifier: a hard-row selector using nonuniform advice proves only a nonuniform row claim unless the advice is charged by multiplexing or removed.
falsifier: a locally checkable dense projection of accepted certificates to useful small-circuit avoidance becomes a natural-property obstruction, not a valid sparse carrier.
falsifier: residual agreement with an easy D_N off polynomially many inputs collapses any claimed N^{1+epsilon} beta-zero lower bound when r<epsilon.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: For alpha_ad<0.64, the upper exponent max{0.48,0.42+alpha_ad,1.03} is below 1.06, so the carrier is invalid. At alpha_ad>=0.64, the low-cover falsifier no longer fires and the proof obligation becomes high adaptive-cover dimension or direct anti-ball soundness.
held_fixed_controls: M_N=N^{0.42+o(1)}, rho=0.48, and beta-zero query length L_N=(log N)^d are fixed.
No advice is allowed in row selection or certificate opening.
Residual size is held at |R_N|<=N^{0.03+o(1)} unless the experiment explicitly crosses the patch threshold.
The target remains the same H_N^{SAT} circuit lower bound, not an auxiliary MCSP language.
gedanken_experiment_design.need_decision: Design now as a falsifier probe for the beta-zero XOR packet.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The route needs a concrete exponent threshold for when MCSP/MKtP certificates produce an upper bound on the exact target family rather than merely sounding weak.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Take H_N^{SAT}(x)=xor_{j<=N^{0.42}} SAT(G_N(x,j)) with L_N=(log N)^d, generator size N^{0.48+o(1)}, and a proposed Psys certificate proving C(H_N^{SAT})>N^{1.06}. The certificate clusters query labels and has an adaptive opener except on R_N.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal opener-to-circuit lemma showing that accepted Psys certificates generate functional SAT labels for all nonresidual outer inputs, plus a same-family residual agreement certificate for H_N^{SAT}.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: Vary the adaptive-cover exponent alpha_ad of the label opener from 0.40 to 0.70.
